questions.title: Dereference Pointer Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n into a variable. Create a pointer to that variable and print the value via the pointer.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The integer n printed via pointer dereference.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer Offset Access Drill
questions.description:
Read three integers a, b, c into a 3-element array, then access the third element (index 2) via pointer arithmetic and print it.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The third integer printed via *(p + 2).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= each integer <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer Array Sum Drill
questions.description:
Read n followed by n integers. Compute the sum of the integers by traversing the array with pointer arithmetic.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The sum of the integers.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= each integer <= 10^4

questions.title: Null Pointer Guard Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n. If n is non-zero, set a pointer p to &n; otherwise set p to NULL. Print the value via *p when p is not NULL, otherwise print "NULL".

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The value of n (when non-zero) or the string "NULL" (when n == 0).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer to Pointer Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n. Create a pointer p pointing to n and a pointer-to-pointer pp pointing to p. Print the value via double dereference **pp.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The value n printed via **pp.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Function Pointer Call Drill
questions.description:
Read two integers a and b. Use a function pointer fp pointing to an add(int, int) helper to compute and print a + b.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The sum a + b computed via fp(a, b).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9

questions.title: Sensor Reading via Pointer
questions.description:
A temperature sensor stores its reading in a variable. Read an integer temperature (in degrees Celsius) and print the value via a pointer, simulating hardware indirection.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer temperature.

Output Format:
The temperature value printed via pointer dereference.

Constraints:
-1000 <= t <= 1000

questions.title: Warehouse Price Index Lookup
questions.description:
A warehouse has 5 item prices stored in an array. Read 5 integers (the prices), then a 0-based index i, and print the price at index i via pointer arithmetic.

Input Format:
Line 1: five space-separated integers.
Line 2: an integer index i (0 <= i <= 4).

Output Format:
The price at index i.

Constraints:
1 <= price <= 10000, 0 <= i <= 4

questions.title: Daily High Temperature Maximum
questions.description:
A weather station records daily high temperatures for n days. Find the maximum temperature using pointer traversal of the array.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers (temperatures).

Output Format:
The maximum temperature.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -1000 <= t <= 1000

questions.title: Bootloader Config Pointer Check
questions.description:
A bootloader reads a flag f and a config value v. If f is 1, the config pointer is set to &v; if f is 0, the pointer stays NULL. Print the dereferenced value when f is 1, otherwise print "FAIL".

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: f and v.

Output Format:
The value v (when f == 1) or "FAIL" (when f == 0).

Constraints:
f in {0, 1}, -10^9 <= v <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer Swap Helper Function
questions.description:
Two players' scores a and b must be exchanged using a helper function that takes two int pointers. Read a and b, then call swap(&a, &b), then print the swapped values separated by a single space.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
The two integers after swapping, space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9

questions.title: In Place Array Reversal via Pointers
questions.description:
A signal processing tool reverses an array of n integers in place using two pointer walkers (lo and hi). Read n and n integers, reverse the array, then print the reversed elements space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The reversed array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= each value <= 10^4

questions.title: Second Largest via Pointer Traversal
questions.description:
Given an array of n distinct integers, find the second largest using pointer traversal. Print the second largest value.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n (n >= 2).
Line 2: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
The second largest integer.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100, all values distinct, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4

questions.title: Pointer Table Lookup Guard
questions.description:
A database stores n integers and exposes them via an array of n pointers (each ptr[i] points to data[i]). Given a 0-based query index q, print the value via the pointer table, or print "NULL" if q is out of range.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: an integer query index q.

Output Format:
The value at index q, or "NULL" if q is out of range.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4, -10^4 <= q <= 10^4

questions.title: Active Setting via Pointer to Pointer
questions.description:
A configuration manager has two settings (a and b). Given a flag f (0 means use a, 1 means use b), set an active pointer to the chosen setting and use a pointer-to-pointer to print the active setting's value.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: a b f.

Output Format:
The value of the active setting.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9, f in {0, 1}

questions.title: Function Pointer Calculator Dispatch
questions.description:
A simple calculator dispatches to one of two operations via a function pointer. Read two integers a and b, and an operator char op ('+' for add, '*' for multiply). Print the result, or "INVALID" for unsupported operators.

Input Format:
A single line with two integers and an operator: "a b op".

Output Format:
The result of a op b, or "INVALID".

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9, op in {'+', '*', others}

questions.title: Pointer Arithmetic Palindrome Check
questions.description:
Check whether an array of n integers is a palindrome (reads the same forward and backward) using two pointer walkers (lo and hi). Read n then n integers, print "Yes" or "No".

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
"Yes" if palindrome, else "No".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4

questions.title: Max Index via Pointer Walk
questions.description:
A streaming service has n subscriber usage values. Find the 0-based index of the maximum usage using pointer arithmetic. If there is a tie, return the smallest index.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The 0-based index of the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4

questions.title: Active Array Sum via Pointer to Pointer
questions.description:
A traffic monitor keeps two parallel arrays A and B (each of n integers). A flag f selects which array is active. Use a pointer-to-pointer to the active array's first element pointer to compute and print the sum of the active array.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n integers for array A.
Line 3: n integers for array B.
Line 4: integer flag f (0 selects A, 1 selects B).

Output Format:
The sum of the active array.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4, f in {0, 1}

questions.title: Dispatch Table of Function Pointers
questions.description:
A dispatch table holds 4 function pointers: add, sub, mul, divide (integer division). Read an operation index op (0..3), two integers a and b, then print the result via the function pointer. Print "ERROR" if op is out of range or if division by zero is attempted.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: op, a, b.

Output Format:
The result, or "ERROR".

Constraints:
op in {-1..5}, -10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9
